fact: The Ministry of Health's statistical yearbook for 2021, produced by its own Sistema de Informação da Saúde (SIS) office, states that the Ministry chose DHIS2 as the management software of the health information system, to produce periodic reports and health bulletins and to serve as the data warehouse fed from source systems, with a web portal for sharing data; no date is given for the choice, so the document's published date is used.

The Ministry of Health's own page for the Sistema de Informação da Saúde states that DHIS2 was officially launched as the health information system on 18 December 2019 in the presence of the Minister of Health, describes it as a web platform for digital forms and indicators, national-level data storage, report generation and aggregate data, and names a SIS coordinator.

The WHO country office reports that during the 2024-2025 biennium DHIS2 was implemented in all districts, strengthening the national health information system for data collection, analysis and use in health services management, and that district health managers were trained on the platform, on data quality and on report generation; no month is given.

WHO reports that in the 2022-2023 biennium it supported the Department of Health Information Systems in drawing up strategies and micro-plans, strengthening use of the DHIS2 tool for data quality with a data validation component, and addressing shortcomings in the daily recording of health data in district health units and in central, district and regional services; the passage places the system with that department and gives no month.

WHO states that it added indicators for monitoring non-communicable diseases to the DHIS2 platform, which is used to collect, validate, analyse and share data on people with communicable and non-communicable diseases, and that integrated disease surveillance and response data are being integrated into DHIS2, while data quality and reliability remain a problem and even paper data collection is weak; the document dates none of this, so the publication date is used.

The WHO country cooperation strategy 2023-2027, approved by the Minister of Health and aligned with the national health development plan, lists implementation of DHIS2 in the districts with data from all health plans and programmes made available as a country-office product under strategic priority 1, budgeted at an estimated USD 4,250,000 over five years for the whole priority, and describes the national strategy for a robust health information system as fragile; dated to publication, the document giving no other date.

The national health development plan states that the Ministry of Health approved the nationwide use of DHIS2 as its health information management system, run by the ministry's SIS unit, and that two years after implementation its use covers only the vaccination, reproductive health, tuberculosis, HIV/AIDS and malaria programmes, with health professionals failing to adhere to it even where it is available; the passages give no date, so the plan's September 2022 date is used.

The Ministry of Health's National Health Development Plan 2023-2032 carries a costed health information pillar that names DHIS2: recognition of DHIS2 by ministerial order as the country's selected system, training of SIS technicians, focal points in health units, equipment for health centres to run DHIS2 and parameterising all programmes on it, while itself recording a weak national strategy and an SIS strategy still to be written; dated to the plan, September 2022.

The plan states that the SIS, still being built, has the support of WHO, Gavi, UNFPA and UNICEF, and lists WHO, UNDP, the Global Fund, UNICEF, the World Bank, UNFPA and Gavi beside the Ministry of Health as implementing partners for its DHIS2 training, support team and equipment; the passages name no domestic budget line, and the date is the plan's, September 2022.

The plan refers to a pilot phase of the single clinical process at the Ayres de Menezes central hospital and the Água Grande Health Area, to be evaluated before expansion to the whole national health system; it does not name the facilities of the health area, and the date is the plan's, September 2022.

The plan describes the single clinical process as in a pilot phase at the Ayres de Menezes Hospital and the Água Grande Health Area, with computerised clinical records to be introduced gradually through a pilot model of health centres and the central hospital; no count of facilities is given, and the date is the plan's, September 2022.

The plan attributes the digital health tools, namely the single clinical process, computerised clinical records and clinical information available on a network, to the Ministry of Health's SIS, which is also the data source for the indicator counting health units with computerised clinical records; dated to the plan, September 2022.

The National Health Development Plan 2023-2032 sets a strategic axis on expanding the single process to the whole national health system, with an evaluation of the pilot, an equipment needs report and purchase of computer equipment, and a further axis on digital health at all levels of care; dated to the plan, September 2022.

The Joint SDG Fund programme's final report, dated 26 July 2022, states that DHIS2 was adopted as the main information software of the Ministry of Health and that the Single Process module for patient files was developed inside it, with field supervision by the ministry's epidemiology directorate and Health Information System.

The report states that the DHIS2 work was paid for by the joint programme with support from the University of Oslo, Gavi and the Global Fund, that the French and Canadian cooperations bought IT material, and that rolling the Single Process out beyond the pilot will be done with funding from other donors; it names no domestic budget for it, as at 26 July 2022.

The report states that IT equipment was bought so that patient data is entered from reception through the nurses and doctors, each patient's file being reached by a bar code sticker and scanner, and that a performance-based incentive was paid to health professionals for capturing data during the transition from paper to online filling; 8 bar code scanners and 2 bar code printers are listed among the equipment, as at 26 July 2022.

The report states that the Single Process has not been rolled out to other districts and that its implementation still needs consolidating in the first pilot district, Água Grande; it gives no count of facilities using it, as at 26 July 2022.
